newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany probes soldiers in Bosnia shooting incident.
newsitem.headline: Germany probes soldiers in Bosnia shooting incident.

text.p: German prosecutors said on Tuesday they were investigating two soldiers on suspicion of manslaughter after two co-servicemen were killed in a shooting incident in Sarajevo last week.

The two soldiers serving in the NATO-led peace force in Bosnia were killed and a third seriously wounded last Friday, when a 20mm cannon mounted on a patrol vehicle fired several rounds and hit an armoured personnel carrier nearby.
State prosecutor Erich Jung his office was investigating a 27-year-old commanding officer and a 22-year-old gunner on suspicion of manslaughter and bodily harm caused by negligence.
Faulty equipment alone could not have been the cause of the accident and it appeared far more likely to have been the result of carelessness, Jung said.

The incident took place near the Rajlovac camp on the outskirts of Sarajevo, which houses some of the German and French soldiers in the 31,000-strong Stabilisation Force (SFOR), policing Bosnia's 1995 peace agreement.
Germany has sent some 2,000 peacekeeping troops to Bosnia, the first deployment abroad of German combat troops since World War Two.
